scopeNote: Sacchi's Milan (1987-91) and Italy (1991-96). Named by sources 'zona-pressing' (a label Sacchi gave his own system according to Van Basten, who disputes its novelty), zonal marking, compact 4-4-2 with at most 25 m between defensive and front line, high line with offside trap, shadow football training. Popular label 'pressing' is not uniform: Sacchi himself describes partial, total and fake pressing; Gullit says full high pressing was not possible in 1987/88 because of the back-pass rule. Italy 1994 is described as fluid 4-4-2/4-1-2-3 with a 4-3 block variant. Partial dates (month or season) used where sources give no day; exact appointment days not found. Set-pieces: no Sacchi-specific source found.
openQuestions: Exact day of Sacchi's appointment at Milan (June/July 1987) not found; start 1987-07-01 is the user's date.
Italy end: user date 1996-06-30; Panorama lists 'in carica ... al 6 novembre 1996'. Appointment announced/contract signed in October 1991, first match 1991-11-13; user start 1991-11-01.

Gullit (SempreMilan 2025) says full high pressing was not possible in 1987/88 due to the back-pass rule, versus sources saying high press from the start; Mannari says early zonal marking 'very slow, without any pressing'.
Distance between lines: 25 m (Coaches' Voice, FIFA, Bleacher Report) versus 15-20 m between the three lines (SempreMilan).
Van Basten says zona-pressing was marketed as revolutionary but was essentially defensive; sources frame it as offensive pressing.
Original Italian wording of the 'fantino/cavallo' quote and of 'la cosa più importante tra le cose meno importanti' not seen; Italian primary sources not found for dated quotes.
Zonal marking novelty: SempreMilan search summary and Mannari mention zonal marking existed (Liedholm's Milan, Roma, Napoli) before Sacchi; Coaches' Voice traces it to Zeze Moreira in 1950s Brazil.
